bottleneck: Releasing engineered microbes to degrade pollutants or capture carbon risks ecological disruption: engineered strains can mutate, transfer genes to wild microbes, or outcompete native species with cascading effects. No biocontainment strategy — kill switches, auxotrophy, or genetic firewalls — has been proven reliable over evolutionary timescales in open environments, where selection pressure finds every weakness. Field release therefore stays effectively prohibited regardless of the potential benefit.
current_state: Bioremediation uses naturally occurring or minimally modified microbes under contained permits. Truly engineered environmental release remains a regulatory non-starter worldwide.
title: No reliable biocontainment for environmental release
why_it_blocks: Engineered microbes could clean pollution and draw down carbon, but ecology cannot be recalled. Without trustworthy containment, environmental synthetic biology stays in the lab while the problems it could solve keep growing.
